decisions.question: How is the phase cut into at most 5 tasks?

options.label: four tasks
options.consequence: 1 the package, its workspace entry and the purity test; 2 topics, topic references, names and scopes; 3 sources, envelopes, lineage, redaction and observers; 4 gate and verification doc. Each declaration task turns a named group of fixtures green; one review sitting fewer than five

options.label: five tasks, observers alone
options.consequence: observers (about 45 lines of interfaces) get their own task and review; the cap is reached for a gate-only phase

options.label: three tasks
options.consequence: every declaration in one task: the surface and reject sets go from 13 failing to green in one step, so a reviewer cannot accept the topic family while rejecting the envelope

decisions.why: The fixtures split cleanly by what they import: topics.dart and six reject libraries need only topic.dart and scope.dart (dry run T2.4: 24 of 30 pass), the other six need the envelope family. Observers are small interfaces whose only fixtures also need MessageEnvelope, so they ride with Task 3. The signal that would have split observers out: a full-review tier.

decisions.question: How are topic-model@v1's declarations split into files under lib/src/topic/ (nidana.model D4 names only the directory)?

options.label: one library per Interface section
options.consequence: seven files: topic.dart (Topics, and Topic references and names), message_source.dart, envelope.dart, lineage.dart, scope.dart, observer.dart, redacted_payload.dart; each sealed family sits in one library as Dart requires; nidana.model.8 fills them section by section

options.label: one file
options.consequence: lib/src/topic/topic_model.dart, the stand-ins' shape; about 300 lines that nidana.model.8 then grows to about 700

options.label: eight files, TopicRef alone
options.consequence: topic_ref.dart for the Topic references and names section; Topic.ref and every observer import it

decisions.why: Files follow the Interface's headings, so a reviewer compares each file with one section. TopicRef and the name predicate share topic.dart because Topic.ref returns a TopicRef and the predicate is about topic names; a separate file would hold 15 lines. The envelope and lineage libraries import each other, which Dart allows.

decisions.question: How does the main library export the declarations: whole files or show lists?

options.label: show lists
options.consequence: export 'src/topic/{file}.dart' show {names}, files in path order, names ascending; the export list names exactly the 25 Interface names, so a helper that nidana.model.8 adds to a src file stays private to the package

options.label: whole files
options.consequence: shorter lines; every public name a later phase adds under lib/src/topic/ becomes public API without an export edit

decisions.why: D3 makes the export lists part of what a type-level phase lands, and nidana.model.5's Verification checks that the public libraries export exactly what the Interfaces list; a show list states that in the file. Cost: nidana.model.4 and .5 add names to the same lines (they collide on the export list anyway).

decisions.question: Which members does a type-level body deliver, and which throw UnimplementedError (D3: every body that computes throws)?

options.label: stored arguments and declaration constants delivered
options.consequence: every getter the reject set assigns to is a final field holding its argument as given; variant returns its class's TopicVariant and valueType returns T; Lineage.root, a const constructor with no body, initializes its constant fields; ref, createInitial, isWellFormedTopicName, tryParse, publishedTo, redacted, causedBy, combine, withLatestFrom, isAtLeastAsLongAs, permits and RedactedPayload.of throw

options.label: throw everywhere a getter is not a field
options.consequence: variant and valueType throw too; a switch on topic.variant in a consumer throws until nidana.model.8, whose scope does not list them

options.label: deliver every trivial body
options.consequence: causedBy and RedactedPayload.of land now; nidana.model.8's scope, which lists them, shrinks and D3 is bent

decisions.chosen: stored arguments and declaration constants delivered
decisions.why: nidana.model.8's scope lists ref, createInitial, causedBy, RedactedPayload.of and the rest, but never variant or valueType, so the node plan expects those two from this phase; each is a constant of its declaration, not a computation. The rule gives the implementer one test: does the body derive a value from arguments or other values?
evidence: hsdd/spec/nidana.model.md D3 and phase nidana.model.8 Scope

decisions.question: The Interface declares toString() on MessageEnvelope (G15) and RedactedPayload (G24), and MessageSource's renderings (G17) are toString too. Does this phase declare them?

options.label: toString stays Object's
options.consequence: like == and hashCode under D3, no override until nidana.model.8; printing or interpolating a value shows Instance of ..., never a throw

options.label: declare toString throwing UnimplementedError
options.consequence: the Interface's toString lines exist now; every string interpolation, debug print and test-failure description of an envelope, source or redacted payload throws until nidana.model.8

decisions.why: D3 keeps the Object members that value semantics override as Object's until the delivering phase; toString is the third of them and its override is G15, G17 and G24 behavior, which nidana.model.8's scope lists (the source renderings, the redacting toString). A throwing toString would break matcher's failure messages in every consumer test. Nothing a surface or reject fixture checks depends on the override.
evidence: hsdd/spec/nidana.model.md D3 and phase nidana.model.8 Scope

decisions.question: Do StateTopic's constructors store initial, and does MessageEnvelope copy parentCorrelationIds, before nidana.model.8 implements createInitial (G9) and the unmodifiable copies (G4)?

options.label: store neither now
options.consequence: initial is a parameter with no field (a private field nobody reads is an unused_field warning under --fatal-infos while createInitial throws); parentCorrelationIds is an initializing formal holding the list as given; nidana.model.8 adds the storage and the copy without changing either signature

options.label: store and copy now
options.consequence: private initial fields with an ignore comment, and List.unmodifiable in the initializer; G4's list half and part of G9 land a phase early

decisions.why: nidana.model.8's scope lists unmodifiable copies of every list (G4) and createInitial (G9). Leaving both out keeps this phase free of suppressions for state it does not read, and the public signatures, which are what the surface and reject sets and every consumer compile against, are identical either way. The Interface's trailing comment `copied, unmodifiable` stays beside the parameter as the contract's statement.
evidence: hsdd/spec/nidana.model.md D3 and phase nidana.model.8 Scope

decisions.question: Lineage.causedBy is a generative constructor whose final fields must be initialized; how does it throw UnimplementedError?

options.label: constant initializers and a throwing body
options.consequence: the four fields take null, null, const [] and false, and the body throws; the signature stays generative as the Interface writes it

options.label: throw in the initializer list
options.consequence: causationId = throw UnimplementedError() leaves the remaining initializers after an expression that never completes

options.label: deliver it
options.consequence: four field reads from cause; G18's causedBy half lands a phase early, against D3

decisions.chosen: constant initializers and a throwing body
decisions.why: It keeps the Interface's generative form and D3's rule with code that reads plainly; the dry run analyzes clean. nidana.model.8 replaces the initializers and drops the body.

decisions.question: RedactedPayload needs final fields typeName and hash (values_are_immutable.dart expects assignment_to_final) and so a private generative constructor, which nothing calls while RedactedPayload.of throws; the root analyze reports it as unused_element (a WARNING). How is the analyzer kept clean?

options.label: an ignore with its reason
options.consequence: one `// ignore: unused_element` above `const RedactedPayload._(this.typeName, this.hash);`, under a line saying RedactedPayload.of constructs through it once nidana.model.8 lands it; nidana.model.8 removes both lines

options.label: implement RedactedPayload.of now
options.consequence: no suppression; G24's computation lands a phase early, against D3 and nidana.model.8's scope

decisions.why: D3 asks for the final field behind every getter and a throwing body together; for a class whose only public constructor is a factory these two leave the private constructor unused. The suppression is the smaller departure, local to one line, and it is the only ignore the plan allows. Observed: the first draft without it reported `warning ... The declaration 'RedactedPayload._' isn't referenced ... unused_element`.

decisions.question: MessageSource's dartdoc in the Interface writes the renderings as 'topology:<id>', 'service:<name>', 'page:<routeOrName>' and 'executor:<name>'; copied as written, the root lint set (lints 6.1.0 recommended) reports four unintended_html_in_doc_comment INFOs, which fail fvm dart analyze --fatal-infos. What does the copy say?

options.label: backtick the renderings
options.consequence: each of the five quoted renderings, unknown included, becomes a code span, quotes kept inside the backticks; every other character is the Interface's; reported as a contract gap so hsdd-contract can make the Interface text match

options.label: ignore_for_file
options.consequence: the dartdoc stays byte-for-byte, under a file-wide suppression of a lint that also guards every later doc comment in message_source.dart

options.label: stop for hsdd-contract
options.consequence: the phase waits on a text touch that changes no semantics

decisions.why: The run rule copies Interface dartdoc as written; the lint makes that impossible for these lines, and a code span is the dartdoc form of literal text, so the reading is unchanged. A file-wide ignore would hide later real defects. The gap does not block: the copy differs only by markup, and an Interface touch would converge on the same text.
evidence: docs/auto-run/experiments/topic-model-declarations-plan/ (first draft analysis: 4 unintended_html_in_doc_comment at message_source.dart lines 4 and 5)

decisions.question: How is the package README worded, given that D4 has nidana.model.3 write it once and no phase is planned to edit it?

options.label: the whole package at 0.1.0
options.consequence: purpose (topics, envelopes and lineage, scopes, observers, redaction, the topology DSL with its recording builder, the IR with graphs, renderers and analyses), the purity promise of G25 and G26, the three public libraries ADR-002 item 3 fixes, one registry example, the license; at this commit two of the three libraries do not exist yet

options.label: only what exists now
options.consequence: topics and envelopes only; true at this commit, stale after nidana.model.4 and .5 unless those phases edit a file D4 says is written once

decisions.why: D4 writes README, CHANGELOG and LICENSE once, and ADR-002 item 3 and D4 fix the three public libraries, so the README can state the package as released without a later edit. No phase-dependent status (UnimplementedError, identity equality) goes in it, because that would go stale at nidana.model.8. The example uses only declarations this phase lands.

decisions.question: What do CHANGELOG.md and the pubspec's description say, and does the pubspec carry homepage or repository?

options.label: minimal, no repository
options.consequence: CHANGELOG `## 0.1.0` then `- Initial version.`, which the release bump rewrites; a one-sentence description of 60 to 180 characters as pub recommends; no homepage or repository field

options.label: per-phase changelog
options.consequence: a line per phase; D4 says no phase edits CHANGELOG.md

decisions.why: D4: no phase edits CHANGELOG.md, which the version bump at release writes. ADR-002 item 9: the repository field and publishing are owner actions outside the tree.

decisions.question: Do the package's own tests stop at purity_test.dart (D6), or does the plan add a test file for the Review Focus lines?

options.label: add declarations_test.dart, lasting facts only
options.consequence: seven tests of what the declarations already fix and nidana.model.8 keeps: G6 defaults, variant and valueType (G6, G7), a computed topic's factory not called at construction (G9), the runtime asserts of G10 and of the non-empty source fields, envelope defaults, Lineage.root (G18's root half); no test pins a throwing body or identity equality

options.label: purity_test.dart alone
options.consequence: the surface and reject sets check types only, so a wrong default or a missing runtime assert would pass this phase's gate unseen until nidana.model.8's behavior replay

decisions.why: writing-plans requires each Review Focus line to get its test in the owning task. Every test here stays true when nidana.model.8 implements the bodies, so no later phase deletes one; asserting UnimplementedError or identity would be churn. `dart test` runs with assertions on (dry run T2.4: the G10 test passes).

decisions.question: How does purity_test.dart read the pubspec and the libraries (D6 fixes what it checks, not how)?

options.label: line readers over the text
options.consequence: a pubspec section reader (keys indented two spaces under a top-level key) instead of package:yaml, which dev_dependencies exactly test excludes and depend_on_referenced_packages would report; import and export directives, single or double quoted, prefixed or not; the forbidden tokens searched over the whole source, comments included; a self-test of the readers

options.label: package:yaml and imports only
options.consequence: a yaml dev dependency breaks G26's own check; export directives unread

decisions.why: G26 makes test the only dev dependency, so the test cannot depend on a YAML parser. An export pulls a library in as an import does. D6 says none contains the tokens, so comments count. Seeded violations (an aliased dart:io import, Timer( in a comment, path as a second dependency) each fail the test (dry run T1.5).

decisions.question: The Interface carries trailing // comments beside members (`// Spec §9.2`, `// non-empty`, `// copied, unmodifiable`, the enum value notes). How are they carried?

options.label: as line comments, as written
options.consequence: they stay beside the field, parameter or value they annotate; dart format realigns their spacing only; the comments on == and hashCode go with the members this phase does not declare

options.label: rewritten as dartdoc
options.consequence: richer API docs, but new text the Interface does not have

decisions.why: The run rule copies Interface text as written; the trailing comments are not dartdoc, so keeping them as comments is the faithful copy.

decisions.question: Routed item: ADR-001 item 4's marker form cannot express two diagnostics on one line, and the structure set rejects stacked markers; how does the plan handle the first real reject replay?

options.label: stop condition, checked in the dry run
options.consequence: Tasks 2 to 4 stop and report a reject line that carries a marked and an unmarked code as a contract gap for hsdd-adr, never working around it; the dry run against the planned declarations reports one code per line in all ten reject libraries, so none is expected

options.label: propose a marker form now
options.consequence: an ADR change before any line needs it

decisions.chosen: stop condition, checked in the dry run
decisions.why: The routed note asks for a stop condition. Experiment step R lists every (line, code) pair the analyzer reports in the ten reject libraries against the planned declarations: no line has two codes, so the gap stays latent for this contract; topology-dsl@v2 and topology-ir@v1 meet the same question at nidana.model.4 and .5.

decisions.question: Which sections does the gate-only verification doc keep: the slim list (gate command, expected output, a 3 to 5 line checklist, Learnings, Sign-off), or the headings the implement gate checks?

options.label: the gate's six headings, slim content, one Metrics line
options.consequence: Commands to run, Expected output, Observed (dated gate output and the checklist), Outstanding, Learnings, Sign-off, all short, plus a one-line Metrics with the product diff against the estimate

options.label: only the slim list
options.consequence: fails impl-gate.mjs implement, which requires Observed and Outstanding headings

decisions.chosen: the gate's six headings, slim content, one Metrics line
decisions.why: docs/auto-run/tools/impl-gate.mjs implement errors on a missing Commands to run, Expected output, Observed, Outstanding, Learnings or Sign-off heading. The Metrics line is optional in the template; it feeds the open checkpoint question about the node's line estimates.

experiments.question: Does the planned task sequence produce the failing and passing outputs the plan states, do the planned declarations pass all 30 topic-model fixtures against the real replay tool with a clean root analyze, does any reject line carry two codes, and does adding the member change the lockfile?

The first draft also showed two facts the governance does not state: RedactedPayload._ is reported as unused_element while RedactedPayload.of throws, and the Interface dartdoc of MessageSource trips unintended_html_in_doc_comment (four INFOs).

contract_gaps.where: hsdd/contract/topic-model.md ## Interface, Message sources: the MessageSource dartdoc renderings 'topology:<id>', 'service:<name>', 'page:<routeOrName>', 'executor:<name>'
contract_gaps.problem: Copied as written (the run rule for Interface dartdoc), the four renderings are reported by the root lint set (package:lints 6.1.0 recommended) as unintended_html_in_doc_comment INFOs, which fail fvm dart analyze --fatal-infos. Non-blocking: the plan backticks them in the copy. No fixture is affected; every committed surface and reject fixture is consistent with the Interface (30 of 30 pass against the planned declarations).
contract_gaps.proposed_fix: hsdd-contract touch, no version bump: put each rendering of the MessageSource dartdoc in a code span, quotes inside the backticks (`'topology:<id>'`, `'service:<name>'`, `'page:<routeOrName>'`, `'executor:<name>'`, `'unknown'`), so the producer's copy is verbatim.

notes_for_orchestrator: Routed item (ADR-001 item 4, two diagnostics on one line) disposition: planned as a stop condition in Global Constraints (Contract gaps), referenced from Tasks 2 to 4; the dry run (output.txt R) reports one code per line in all ten topic-model reject libraries against the planned declarations, so no gap for topic-model@v1. Carry the item on to nidana.model.4 and .5, whose reject sets are still unreplayed.

Learning for the verification doc and the owner: nidana.model.3's Scope says the package joins the lockfile, but adding the member leaves pubspec.lock byte-identical (a workspace lockfile records no member; meta 1.19.0 and test were already transitive). The plan commits pubspec.lock only if git shows it modified.

Learning: D3 (final field behind every getter, throwing bodies) leaves RedactedPayload._ unused while RedactedPayload.of throws; the plan carries one // ignore: unused_element, which nidana.model.8 removes when it lands RedactedPayload.of. Worth a line in nidana.model.8's plan.

For nidana.model.6's plan: against these declarations topic-model@v1's behavior binding already loads and analyzes clean (output.txt B); 9 cases pass and 32 fail, not all on UnimplementedError: some fail on identity equality or on Object.toString (for example Expected topology:checkout-flow, Actual Instance of TopologySource). nidana.model.6's Verification sentence (cases fail on UnimplementedError, not on loading) holds only loosely.

For nidana.model.8's plan: it must add StateTopic's initial storage, the unmodifiable copy of MessageEnvelope.parentCorrelationIds, the ==, hashCode and toString overrides, and replace Lineage.causedBy's placeholder initializers; the package tests of this phase (declarations_test.dart, purity_test.dart) pin only facts that stay true after it.

The experiment keeps a draft pubspec.yaml named nidana_dart_contracts under docs/ (excluded from the root analyze by docs/**, not a workspace member); run.sh copies it into a temporary workspace only.
Commit scope in the plan: feat(dart_contracts), following the contract_check precedent (package name without nidana_).
